title: Restoring an Urban River
paragraphs: After decades of industrial pollution rendered a river running through his city essentially lifeless, Bagas joined a coalition advocating for restoration despite widespread public skepticism that meaningful improvement was realistically achievable given the accumulated damage.

Initial testing revealed contamination levels considerably worse than public records had suggested, prompting some coalition members to question whether the restoration goal itself was genuinely realistic within any practical timeframe.

Rather than abandoning the ambitious goal, the coalition adjusted its approach, focusing initially on smaller, measurable improvements rather than promising complete restoration within an unrealistic timeframe that risked eventual public disappointment.

Nearly a decade later, with measurable improvements in water quality and returning aquatic life, Bagas reflects that sustained, incremental progress, rather than a single dramatic transformation, ultimately proved more achievable and more genuinely sustainable.
